statements.quote: In parallel, behavioral and qualitative data, including AI prompt histories, submitted solutions, and interview transcripts, were thematically analyzed for evidence of reframing and adaptive reasoning.

statements.quote: To address this, we conducted supplementary robustness analyses treating accommodation as a continuous variable. These analyses confirmed that the primary effects reported in this study remain consistent, strengthening our confidence in the findings.

statements.quote: To enhance transparency and replicability, we have moved the detailed measurement instruments to Appendix A, which provides the full list of survey items used for assimilation, accommodation, emotional engagement, digital literacy, and control variables. This ensures future scholars can replicate or extend our approach.
statements.locator: PDF p. 6 (index 5), Methodology, Measures, final paragraph referring to Appendix A; Markdown line 245.

statements.quote: To examine the mediating role of cognitive strategy, we conducted causal mediation analyses using the PROCESS macro (Model 4), with bootstrapped confidence intervals (5000 resamples) for each innovation outcome. Moderated mediation models (PROCESS Model 7) were then employed to test whether emotional engagement moderated the relationship between cognitive strategy and performance. We expected accommodation to yield higher-quality solutions through increased positive affect, particularly in team-based conditions.

statements.quote: Finally, qualitative data (prompt sequences, team transcripts, and interview reflections) were thematically coded using a structured scheme for reframing, reinterpretation, and role adaptation.

notes:
Classification: on_request. The paper explicitly makes its data available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request (PDF p. 9), and no relevant public deposit was confirmed. No author was contacted and no access request or account was created. The deposits list excludes unrelated search hits and the published article itself; neither constitutes a deposit of c876 study S1 records.

Source coverage: read all 625 lines of the 11-page published article's Markdown conversion, including Appendix A and references. Confirmed relevant passages against the PDF with PyMuPDF, inspected all external PDF hyperlink annotations, and checked for embedded files (none). The form contains no actual data or code URL. No preregistration, repository identifier, external appendix, downloadable analysis code, or external supplementary-file link is stated in the paper. The mention of supplementary robustness analyses (p. 5) describes additional analyses, not a supplementary-file deposit. Appendix A (p. 10) supplies survey instruments; it contains no participant observations. Acknowledgments (p. 10) describe funding only. The PROCESS macro and Software/Data curation authorship credit are mentioned, but neither provides study-specific code.

The published tables contain aggregate statistics. The illustrative participant reflections and prompt examples on p. 7 are not a complete participant/output corpus with identifiers and arm assignments. No confirmed public data permit computing additional per-person arm means, SDs, SEs, analyzed headcounts, dyad-aware contrasts, or diversity measures. Consequently what_we_could_compute is null: final.open_items concerning dyad membership/aggregation, model samples/specifications/coding, direct team contrasts, rater aggregation, allocation procedures, and participant flow cannot be resolved from a confirmed public dataset. The control-training protocol also remains unavailable.
